newsitem.title: LEBANON: Italian Toto bids for Lebanon $35 mln road.
newsitem.headline: Italian Toto bids for Lebanon $35 mln road.

text.p: The Lebanese government is assessing tenders by 13 international firms to build a four km (2.5 mile) stretch of road in east Lebanon, an official source said on Thursday.

"We opened the tenders yesterday. The lowest bid was submitted by Italian firm Toto for about $35 million. We need to further audit the cost estimates in the tender before awarding the contract," the official said.
He said bids ranged between $35 million and $46 million. The government had estimated the cost of the project at $40 million.

The project involves construction of a highway linking the eastern town of Sawfar in Mount Lebanon to the Mdeirij area in the eastern Bekaa Valley. It includes the construction of three overpasses, one 54 metres high.
Last June the government decided to establish a $350 million private toll road company to build a motorway to Syria and ringroads around Beirut at an estimated cost of $1.2 billion.
"The firm that is going to carry out the $35 million project, probably Toto, can eventually become a shareholder in the toll road company," the official added.
